addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- add-contact: Create one CRM Contact via add-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a person with optional Org affiliations. For multi-entity free text, use add-lead.
- add-editorial-carousel: Generate a branded LinkedIn carousel (document post) for a piece from the BGA carousel skeleton. Composes N portrait 4:5 pages from the piece narrative (Why/How/What) using page-type primitives (cover, bullets, term, flow, compare, synth, cta - §5.8 catalogue), renders each page for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, delivers a swipeable PDF, wires it back into the piece `## Visuels`. Use when the user wants a carousel, a document post, or a live retex repurposed as swipeable pages.
- add-editorial-idea: Capture a new editorial idea (LinkedIn post, article, talk seed) as an anchor in `02-Areas/Éditorial/Ideas/`. Runs dedup check, applies frontmatter schema, enforces BGA brand conformity, updates MoC. Auto-detects express vs standard mode. Use when the user wants to capture, add, save, or register an editorial idea, post idea, article idea, or content seed.
- add-editorial-piece: Transform an editorial anchor (`Ideas/<file>.md`) into a piece for a given format (linkedin, article, live, podcast, talk). Resolves the anchor, fills frontmatter from template SSoT, drafts the body, runs brand conformity, ticks the matching line in the anchor's Déclinaisons checklist. Use when the user wants to draft a LinkedIn post, article, talk, live, or podcast piece from an existing idea.
- add-editorial-slides: Generate a branded HTML slide deck for a piece from the BGA slides skeleton. Composes slides from the piece narrative (Why/How/What, key points, tables) using slide-type primitives (title, bullets, cards, table, flow, callout, def, compare, probe, layers - §5.7 catalogue) selected per idea via the §5.7 archetype heuristic, renders each slide for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, wires the deck back into the piece. Interactive HTML opened in the browser, no delivery PNG. Use when the user wants intro slides, a live deck, or a talk/workshop deck for an editorial piece.
- add-editorial-visual: Generate a branded editorial visual (square post visual or LinkedIn event banner) for a piece from the BGA HTML skeleton. Reads the piece's `## Visuels` brief (format + disposition + setup/Why + contenu/How + synthèse/What), composes with CSS auto-layout (never hand-placed coordinates), renders HTML->PNG via Playwright, gates on visual legibility + brand-review, wires the asset back into the piece. Use when the user wants a schema, diagram, before/after, lifecycle visual, or event banner for a LinkedIn post, article, or live.
- add-formation: Bootstrap a new BGA formation by aggregating N editorial anchors (`Ideas/*.md`) into a curriculum. Creates the formation folder, generates the index from template, scaffolds one module file per anchor, backlinks each anchor via its Déclinaisons checklist, updates the Formations MoC. Supports direct mode (--ideas arg) or interactive mode (anchor picker grouped by pillar). Use when the user wants to create, scaffold, build, or initialize a training, workshop, masterclass, or curriculum.
- add-interaction: Create one CRM Interaction (dated exchange report) via add-interaction.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use to log a call/meeting/email/event tied to an Opp or Org.
- add-lead: Add a new prospect (Organisation + optional Opportunity + optional Contact) to the CRM. Accepts free text and/or LinkedIn URLs. Use when the user mentions a new company or contact to add.
- add-opportunity: Create one CRM Opportunity via add-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a new channel/deal on an existing or new target Org. One Opp = one channel.
- add-organisation: Create one CRM Organisation via add-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a single company (no opportunity/contact). For multi-entity free text + LinkedIn, use add-lead.
- archive-opportunity: Move a closed CRM Opportunity (perdu/gagne) to Opportunities/_archive/ via archive-opp.py (git mv, FK-safe). Use to declutter active pipeline after a deal closes.
- archive-project: Guided PARA archival of a finished project. Extracts forward-looking artefacts BEFORE the move - active backlog to Projects, living doc/SSoT to an existing or newly-created Area, structural decisions to ADRs, pure reference to Resources - sets the frozen marker, git mv to 04-Archives, propagates orphan wikilinks. Judgment-heavy (classify + route); writes = git mv + targeted edits. Use when a project is done and must be archived.
- brand-review: Audit a BGA editorial artifact (text and/or visual) against brand SSoT. Verifies tone-of-voice principles, format specs, color tokens, WCAG ratios, text/visual coherence. Outputs a status table + one prioritized recommendation.
- parse-td-results: Parse a Tutorial Dojo HTML exam result, extract incorrect questions, and append summaries to the AWS SAP Mistakes note.
- synthesize-interaction: Synthesize a freelance prospection Interaction draft - restructure the raw note and propagate to the linked Opportunity/Organisation. Thick orchestrator - LLM synthesis only, writes delegated to deterministic scripts.
- update-contact: Update an existing CRM Contact via update-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set personal fields, append Org affiliations or notes.
- update-lead: Quick update of an existing Organisation or Opportunity from free text (informal conversation, phone call, ad-hoc info). Auto-detects the target. Use when the user reports info about an existing prospect.
- update-opportunity: Update an existing CRM Opportunity (non-status fields) via update-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). For status/lost/won transitions use transition-opp.
- update-organisation: Update an existing CRM Organisation via update-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set durable company fields or append to body regions.
- weekly-actions: Display prospection actions for the current calendar week (Mon-Sun), including overdue items. Source - Opportunities. Use when the user asks for actions, planning, or prospection to-do.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Demo run-of-show tasks - live Terraform deferred actions.
# The terraform version lives per sub-dir (01-before/ = 1.15.6, 02-after/ = 1.16-alpha)
# in each sub-dir's mise.toml. Tasks here `cd` into a sub-dir and use `mise exec --
# terraform` so the version re-resolves from that sub-dir (same source as live typing:
# cd + bare terraform), robust in the non-interactive task shell.
# Run with `mise run <task>`; list them with `mise tasks`. Tasks run in a subshell,
# so the `cd` never leaks into your interactive shell.
# (tflint/trivy inherited from the repo-root mise.toml.)

[tasks.init]
description = "init both dirs (once, before the demo)"
run = [
  "cd 01-before && mise exec -- terraform init",
  "cd 02-after  && mise exec -- terraform init",
]

[tasks.versions]
description = "prove the resolved version per dir (show it on screen)"
run = [
  "cd 01-before && mise exec -- terraform version | head -1",

Usage: terraform [global options] graph [options]
  Produces a representation of the dependency graph between different
  objects in the current configuration and state.
  By default the graph shows a summary only of the relationships between
  resources in the configuration, since those are the main objects that
  have side-effects whose ordering is significant. You can generate more
  detailed graphs reflecting Terraform's actual evaluation strategy
  by specifying the -type=TYPE option to select an operation type.
  The graph is presented in the DOT language. The typical program that can
  read this format is GraphViz, but many web services are also available
  to read this format.
Options:
  -plan=tfplan        Render graph using the specified plan file instead of the
                      configuration in the current directory. Implies -type=apply.
  -draw-cycles        Highlight any cycles in the graph with colored edges.
                      This helps when diagnosing cycle errors. This option is
                      supported only when illustrating a real evaluation graph,
                      selected using the -type=TYPE option.
  -type=TYPE          Type of operation graph to output. Can be: plan,
                      plan-refresh-only, plan-destroy, or apply. By default
                      Terraform just summarizes the relationships between the
                      resources in your configuration, without any particular
                      operation in mind. Full operation graphs are more detailed
                      but therefore often harder to read.
  -module-depth=n     (deprecated) In prior versions of Terraform, specified the
                      depth of modules to show in the output.
  -var 'foo=bar'      Set a value for one of the input variables in the root
                      module of the configuration. Use this option more than
                      once to set more than one variable.
  -var-file=filename  Load variable values from the given file, in addition
                      to the default files terraform.tfvars and *.auto.tfvars.
                      Use this option more than once to include more than one
                      variables file.
  -format=FORMAT      Output format for the graph. Supported values are
                      dot (default) and mermaid.

content.text:
`terraform graph -format=mermaid` confirmé sur **1.16.0-beta2**.

**Setup** (sans toucher aux pins du repo, `mise exec` suffit) :
```bash
mise install terraform@1.16.0-beta2
cd ~/git/oss/terraform-examples/examples/terraform-module-testing
mise exec terraform@1.16.0-beta2 -- terraform init
mise exec terraform@1.16.0-beta2 -- terraform graph -format=mermaid
```

**Sortie** (graphe de config par défaut) :
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph module.bucket
    module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket.this["aws_s3_bucket.this"]
    module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.this["aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.this"]
    module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.this["aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.this"]
    module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_versioning.this["aws_s3_bucket_versioning.this"]
  end
  module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.this --> module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket.this
  module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.this --> module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket.this
  module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket_versioning.this --> module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket.this
```

Ce qui change vs le DOT historique (`digraph G { rankdir="RL" ... }`) : rendu natif dans GitHub, Obsidian, Notion, sans GraphViz ni service tiers. Le flag est `-format=dot|mermaid`, documenté dans `terraform graph -help`.

Deux points pour un usage live :
- `-type=plan` produit bien du mermaid aussi, mais les nœuds sont identifiés par pointeur mémoire (`96129417307432[...]`) et les guillemets sont échappés en `"`. Illisible en démo, à garder pour le debug de cycles.
- Le graphe de config par défaut est le seul lisible à l'écran.

Artefacts laissés : `.terraform/` + lockfile dans `examples/terraform-module-testing/` (gitignorés, working tree propre hors ta modif préexistante sur `terraform-check-conditional-policy/s3.tf`).
